Start detached work, then ask what happened to it: whether it is running, what
it exited with, and what it printed. Starting a job also holds an activity
lease for its lifetime, so the environment reports as busy and idle-stop
leaves it alone while the work runs.

Usage:
  erun job [command]

Available Commands:
  attach      Give work started another way a job handle and an activity lease
  await       Wait a bounded time for a job to finish, reporting a timeout distinctly
  cancel      Signal a running job's work by its recorded process, never by pattern
  output      Read a job's captured output, including while it is still running
  start       Run a command, or an AI agent, as a detached job and return its handle
  status      Report one job's state and outcome, or every retained job

Flags:
  -h, --help   help for job

Global Flags:
      --output string   Result format: text (default, human stream) or json (structured result on stdout for orchestrators). (default "text")
      --time            Print the elapsed runtime after the command finishes.
  -v, --verbose count   Increase verbosity: -v streams external tool output, -vv adds erun command traces.

Use "erun job [command] --help" for more information about a command.
